policyNote: These numeric rectangles are conservative Framewright policy, not official permanent platform pixel specifications. Platform UI varies by device, app version, caption length and interactive surface. Re-validate periodically and keep the source/date with every profile version.

generic.basis: Existing Framewright vertical semantic safe area; control only.

youtube_shorts.basis: YouTube documents dynamic visual guides/non-safe areas around viewer controls; numeric insets are our conservative policy, not official pixels.

instagram_reels.basis: Meta recommends keeping key Reels elements in a safe zone and provides a checker; public guidance does not expose one permanent organic pixel rectangle. Numeric insets are our conservative policy.

tiktok.basis: TikTok documents fixed FYP UI occlusion and provides UI/device simulation; numeric insets are our conservative policy, not official pixels.

sources.evidence: Shorts visual guides show where like, comments and description may appear; near-edge overlays can be marked non-safe and partially hidden on some devices.
TikTok UI simulation is provided to test safe-zone area, with separate device-resolution simulation.
FYP fixed UI elements can block creative; important elements should stay in the safe zone. Used for UI topology, not numeric organic pixel dimensions.
Meta recommends 9:16 Reels with key creative elements in the safe zone and provides a safe-zone checker. Used for safe-zone principle, not a claimed permanent organic pixel rectangle.
